name: KeyboardShortcut
description: Renders a keyboard shortcut as a row of small key caps, from explicit keys or from a ShortcutActivator, with an optional app-wide label override.

fields.keyPadding: EdgeInsetsGeometry? - null = symmetric(6, 2) (dashcn px-1.5 py-0.5; h-5 with the text-xs line)
fields.keyBackground: ThemedColor? - null = per variant: the muted token (subtle) or none (ghost)
fields.keyBorderRadius: BorderRadiusGeometry? - null = fixed 4 px (preset-independent kbd rounding)
fields.keyTextStyle: TextStyle? - merged onto the default; null = text-xs (12 on a 16px line, w500) in the ambient mono face
fields.variant: KbdVariant? - null = subtle (muted fill); ghost paints no fill

notes: `KeyboardShortcutDisplayBuilder`, `KeyboardShortcutDisplayHandle` and `shortcutActivatorToKeySet` are already owned by `foundation/keyboard.dart`; the component's local copies are gone.
`KeyboardDisplay` / `KeyboardKeyDisplay` are now `KeyboardShortcut` / `KeyboardKeyCap`, matching the component id.

`KeyboardShortcutDisplayMapper` (a StatefulWidget whose state only cached a handle) becomes `KeyboardShortcutDisplayScope`, a stateless `Data` provider, and is optional: a cap outside it falls back to `defaultKeyboardKeyLabel`.
Key glyphs are not localized copy: a shortcut has to read the same on every keyboard the user is on, so they are a lookup table plus Flutter's own `keyLabel`.
